stem.text: The function f is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of f are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 1 < c < 9 \), for which \( f(c) = 5 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: No. Every tabulated value of f is less than 5, so the Intermediate Value Theorem does not apply on \( [1, 9] \).

worked_solution.text: Because f is differentiable, f is continuous on \( [1, 9] \).
Every tabulated value of f is less than 5, so no two of them have 5 between them.

The Intermediate Value Theorem needs 5 to lie between two values of f, so it guarantees nothing here, and a differentiable f with these values can stay less than 5 throughout. So no such c must exist.

options.label: No. Every tabulated value of f is less than 5, so the Intermediate Value Theorem does not apply on \( [1, 9] \).
Yes. A continuous function on \( [1, 9] \) takes every value between its values, so f takes the value 5.
